claims.text: A machine-learning model trained on HEA data containing atomic-scale descriptors will identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity materials more accurately than empirical or conventional ab initio methods.
The target high-entropy alloys are single-phase, disordered materials spanning diverse compositions and microstructures.
The model is trained using experimental and computed data concerning phonon transport and atomic-scale disorder.
The proposed operating domain extends from ambient to moderately elevated temperatures.
Phonon dispersion, local lattice distortions, and mass or bonding disorder govern phonon scattering in the target alloys.
Machine learning can exploit nonlinear relationships between composition and atomic-scale phonon-transport phenomena.
Learning these nonlinear relationships will improve predictions of low thermal conductivity.
The model will reduce prediction error by approximately 20% relative to the baseline methods.
The conventional ab initio methods used as baselines do not directly account for local disorder.
The model is expected to be reliable only for HEAs compositionally and structurally similar to its training data.
The model may not generalize to alloys containing significant secondary phases or extrinsic microstructural defects.
The magnitude of the prediction improvement may vary among HEA systems.
